A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same controlled MLM-versus-CLM pretraining study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original experiments involving 38 pretrained models and downstream evaluations, with empirical outcomes in Sections 3–5 and Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and their outcomes, including dataset-level results in Tables 2–17 and supplementary plots in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The model architectures, CLM and MLM objectives, sequential CLM+MLM procedure, and pretraining-from-scratch and continued-pretraining workflows remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use FineWeb-Edu pretraining and the same 12 downstream datasets covering sequence classification, token classification, question answering, and retrieval. Appendix B retains the same language subsets and evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same MLM-only, CLM-only, sequential CLM+MLM, and continued-pretraining comparisons. No evaluated comparator is added, removed, or substantively revised.

E3.justification: Section 2 and Appendices A–B retain the same model sizes, training budgets, masking ratios, data splits, fine-tuning procedures, and evaluation metrics. Changes to dashes in training-ratio notation are typographic.

E4.justification: The analyses of masking ratios, model scale, training duration, fine-tuning sensitivity, and continued pretraining are unchanged. Appendix D retains the same FLOPs comparison, 1B-scale experiment, and loss curves.

E5.justification: Both versions report five fine-tuning seeds and 95% confidence intervals. The standard-deviation reporting in Figures 5 and 7 and uncertainty reporting throughout the appendix tables are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 2–17 contain identical numerical results and uncertainty values, and the rendered plots retain the same findings. No result entries, rankings, or qualitative observations are added or removed.

T1.justification: The CLM and MLM mathematical objectives in Equations 1–2 and their definitions are unchanged. Neither version adds further formal assumptions, proofs, or derivations relative to the other.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about MLM's general performance advantage, CLM's data efficiency and stability, and the benefits of sequential CLM-to-MLM training.

C2.justification: The interpretations of bidirectional context, token-level performance, and training stability remain unchanged. Section 8 retains the same limitations concerning scale, fixed design choices, language coverage, and contrastive post-training.

D1.justification: Architecture specifications, hyperparameters, hardware, compute costs, data-processing details, and documented model/code access information remain unchanged in Section 2, Appendix A, and the reproducibility statement.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Correcting 'ModernBert' to 'ModernBERT' in Section 6 changes capitalization only.

P1.justification: v4 makes limited copyedits: it removes an unnecessary abstract comma, corrects 'on equal amount' to 'on an equal amount' and 'sourced form' to 'sourced from', and normalizes capitalization and hyphenation. Section and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 10's caption loses a stray 'M.', and Figures 1 and 11 receive hyphenation edits. These produce small caption and line-wrapping changes; figure designs, axes, legends, table structures, and placement remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 provides slight editorial polish through grammatical fixes and caption cleanup, including Appendix B and Figure 10. The scientific evidence, explanatory content, limitations, and reproducibility information are unchanged, so these cosmetic corrections do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
